newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich calls end to "tiresome" leadership fight.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich calls end to "tiresome" leadership fight.

text.p: U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich called on Wednesday for an end to turmoil in the Republican Party over his leadership, which he called a "tiresome and overwrought saga".
He issued a statement on the leadership question as divided and anxious Republicans, who hold a narrow majority in the House, began the first of two crucial meetings expected to focus on the issue.
"I strongly encourage every Republican to participate in this dialogue," Gingrich said.
"Let me emphasise: I will not allow another chapter to be written in this tiresome and overwrought saga. This discussion will be the end of the story."

He issued the statement before a closed-door Republican conference originally designed to discuss strategy for passage of balanced budget and tax cut bills, central goals of the party for this congressional session.

But the meeting was overshadowed by the leadership issue, which has dominated Republican activity in the House since reports surfaced last week of an attempt to oust Gingrich by dissatisfied members -- including some leaders -- who felt he had lost the political initiative to President Bill Clinton, a Democrat.
The 228 Republican House members have also been called by Gingrich to another meeting on Wednesday evening to "hold a family discussion on how we can continue to move our party forward as a family."

Gingrich said in his statement: "We must ensure that every member understands both the responsibilities of leaders of the conference and the equally important and commensurate responsibilities of the members of this conference."
Gingrich urged members on Tuesday not to seek the resignation of any leaders who might have been involved in the attempt to oust him.
